title: Chiral Damping-Induced Chirality Switching and Control of Domain Walls in Antiferromagnets
authors: Collins Ashu Akosa, Mu-Kun Lee, Aurélien Manchon, Masahito Mochizuki
abstract: We investigate the impact of chiral damping (CD) on current-driven domain-wall (DW) dynamics in antiferromagnets (AFMs). Asymmetric CD between sublattices generates off-diagonal components in the DW mass tensor, thereby coupling translational and rotational modes. When CD is modulated by an ac gate voltage via the Rashba spin-orbit interaction (RSOI), symmetric and asymmetric contributions induce oscillations in the DW velocity and tilt angle, respectively. A perturbative analysis yields explicit expressions for the oscillation amplitudes, in quantitative agreement with numerical simulations. Remarkably, even in the absence of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), asymmetric CD enables chirality switching between Néel- and Bloch-type DWs. Finally, by exploiting the relativistic Lorentz contraction of the DW width at high driving currents, we propose an experimentally viable protocol to qualitatively and quantitatively extract the CD contribution. These results establish clear experimental signatures of CD in antiferromagnetic DW dynamics and demonstrate its potential as a control parameter for magnetic textures.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates the role of chiral damping in controlling domain wall dynamics within antiferromagnets. By analyzing coupled equations of motion, the authors show that CD introduces coupling between translational and rotational modes, leading to measurable oscillations in DW velocity and tilt angle. The findings establish CD as a key control parameter for manipulating magnetic textures, even enabling chirality switching without DMI.
main_problem: The study investigates how chiral damping (CD) affects current-driven domain wall (DW) dynamics in antiferromagnets (AFMs), aiming to establish measurable experimental signatures for CD.
main_result: Asymmetric CD can induce rich dynamical phenomena, including oscillations in DW velocity and tilt angle, and enables chirality switching between Néel- and Bloch-type DWs even without the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI).
method: The authors employ a perturbative analysis on the coupled equations of motion for the DW center position ($X$) and tilt angle ($\phi$), derived from the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-Slonczewski equation.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a one-dimensional uniaxial AFM domain wall composed of two magnetic sublattices, driven by spin currents (STT/SOT) and subject to chiral damping effects arising from Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit interactions.
key_observables: DW velocity ($v(t)$), tilt angle ($\phi(t)$), oscillation amplitudes ($\delta v$, $\delta\phi$), and the effective mass tensor renormalization.
important_parameters: Chiral damping constants ($ ar{\alpha}_{m,n}^c$), Rashba/Dresselhaus SOI strengths ($\Lambda_R, \Lambda_D$), driving currents (STT/SOT), and external fields ($H_{D0}, \Omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on perturbative expansions in the CD parameters and assumes that spin pumping effects are negligible; it also neglects distortions due to dynamic DW width.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate numerical results showing oscillatory behavior of velocity and tilt angle when oscillating CDs are applied, and demonstrate the transition towards Bloch-like DWs when DMI is absent but asymmetric CD is present.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the governing equations for AFM DW dynamics incorporating CD. It then analyzes how CD couples translational and rotational modes, deriving explicit expressions for oscillatory amplitudes under time-varying driving forces (e.g., oscillating DMI).
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework connecting microscopic dissipation mechanisms (CD) to macroscopic control parameters of magnetic textures in AFMs, which is highly relevant for understanding spintronics and emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter.
